# readme-lint rubric (v1.1.0)

40 rules, 193 weighted points.

## Hero - what a stranger sees in the first screenful

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HERO001` | 6 | all | Exactly one H1 title |
| `HERO002` | 8 | all | A one-sentence tagline directly under the title |
| `HERO003` | 6 | all | Three to five live badges, one style |
| `HERO004` | 4 | all | A navigation row of in-page or sibling-doc links |
| `HERO005` | 8 | all | Visual proof above the fold |
| `HERO006` | 2 | all | A rule separating the hero from the body |

## Orientation - what it is, who it is for, what it is not

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ORI001` | 8 | all | A 'what it is' section that opens on the problem |
| `ORI002` | 6 | all | Verb-led capability bullets in parallel form |
| `ORI003` | 6 | all | An honest scope callout |
| `ORI004` | 3 | all | A table of contents once the page is long |
| `SEC001` | 8 | all | Every section this profile requires is present |

## Onboarding - the path from zero to a working thing

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ONB001` | 9 | all | An install section with a copy-pasteable command |
| `ONB002` | 7 | all | A quickstart that shows real commands and output |
| `ONB003` | 5 | all | Requirements stated before the install command |
| `ONB004` | 4 | all | A way to verify the install worked |
| `ONB005` | 3 | cli, service | A non-interactive path for scripts and CI |
| `ONB006` | 4 | cli, service, app, library | A configuration section with one-shot examples |

## Depth - the reasons behind the features

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DEP001` | 6 | all | A feature tour that stays collapsed by default |
| `DEP002` | 7 | all | Feature bullets that carry their reason |
| `DEP003` | 5 | cli, service, library, docs | An architecture summary that links to the long version |
| `DEP004` | 4 | cli, service, library, docs | An annotated layout tree |
| `DEP005` | 3 | cli, service, app | Paths: where the thing installs itself |

## Trust - contribution, provenance, licence

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TRU001` | 6 | all | A development section with the exact gate commands |
| `TRU002` | 4 | all | A licence section or link |
| `TRU003` | 3 | all | Links out to the deeper documents |
| `TRU004` | 3 | all | A CI badge backed by a workflow that exists |

## Mechanics - links, anchors, alt text, fences

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MEC001` | 8 | all | Every relative link resolves to a file that exists |
| `MEC002` | 6 | all | Every in-page anchor matches a real heading |
| `MEC003` | 5 | all | Every image has alt text |
| `MEC004` | 4 | all | Every fenced block declares its language |
| `MEC005` | 3 | all | Heading levels do not skip |
| `MEC006` | 3 | all | Shell blocks are pasteable |
| `MEC007` | 2 | all | Bare URLs are linked |

## Hygiene - the things that make a README look assembled

| Rule | Weight | Profiles | Wants |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HYG001` | 6 | all | No placeholder text left in |
| `HYG002` | 4 | all | No vanity badges |
| `HYG003` | 4 | all | Claims are specific, not superlative |
| `HYG004` | 2 | all | One bullet marker throughout |
| `HYG005` | 3 | all | Headings are words, not emoji |
| `HYG006` | 3 | all | The page stays inside a readable length |
| `HYG007` | 2 | all | Absolute self-links use relative paths |


## Levels

| Level | Effect on the score | Effect on `--strict` |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | the rule's full weight is lost | exit 1 |
| `warn` | the rule's full weight is lost | — |
| `info` | 40% of the rule's weight is lost | — |

A rule that produces only `info` findings still earns most of its weight, which
is why a good README lands in the nineties rather than at 100. The last few
points are suggestions, not defects.

## Turning a rule off

```json
{ "disable": ["HERO005", "DEP004"] }
```

in `.awesome-readme.json`. Disabled rules leave the denominator, so switching
off a rule you fail raises the score. That is the reason the list lives in a
committed file, where the next person can see the decision.

`readme_lint.py --explain <RULE>` prints the reasoning behind any single rule.
